entries.subject: PDS SN263 V1.0
entries.finding: The retained native alpha-mesh and unseen-facet labels were examined with the body’s source interpretation. The selected source is the primary component: 1148 vertices and 2292 faces in km. The original 2008 radar/light-curve observations control the scientific date, despite the landing page’s conflicting 2003 summary. Exact mesh volume is a model measurement, not a more precise observation than the published 2.5 ±0.3 km diameter.

entries.subject: Becker et al. (2015)
entries.finding: Becker 2015 Table 4 was examined: Alpha equivalent diameter 2.5 ±0.3 km, volume 8.2 ±1.1 km³, period 3.4256 ±0.0002 h and pole (309°, −80°) ±15°. These constraints support the retained model; its precisely computed volume is not an independent, more accurate physical measurement. The table separates Alpha from outer Beta and inner Gamma.

entries.subject: Fang et al. (2011)
entries.finding: Fang 2011 identifies Gamma as the inner companion (semimajor axis 3.804 km) and Beta as the outer companion (16.633 km). The inspected orbital discussion supports component identity and records a possible mutual-plane tilt. It does not qualify a present rotation phase or justify treating an orbital pole as a measured spin pole.

entries.subject: Native radar coverage list
entries.finding: The original a153591alpha_unseen label identifies 96 one-based facet IDs that were never seen below 60° emission angle. This is a concrete source constraint distinct from missing optical imagery; the shared grid does not communicate radar confidence. A future coverage view must bind those IDs to the full source mesh before simplification. Ninety-six facets is not an observed surface-area percentage.
entries.revisitWhen: The existing scientific-data preparation qualifies this source facet list as a distinct coverage view while preserving its angular threshold and facet correspondence.
